Subject: KV-cache regression: exec synthesis & QBR packet inputs

Team —

Summary (TL;DR): On 2027-11-30 we observed a KV-cache degradation that increased median tail latency for text-gen requests and triggered a short SLA window where we missed the 99th percentile by ~1.8x for ~42 minutes. Customer-visible errors were limited to timeouts for a small set of high-concurrency flows (not full returns). Impacted customers include Acme AI (renewal window Q1).

Why this matters for QBR: the QBR packet needs a 1-slide executive summary of what happened, root cause, mitigations, and open owners/ETAs. I pulled the postmortem draft and attached the artifacts (latency traces + full write-up).

Immediate fixes applied:
- Backed out the runtime KV eviction change (rollforward) at 2027-11-30 02:14 UTC — mitigated tail behavior.
- Hotfix improved cache warmup (deployed 02:47 UTC).
- Temporary routing policy: route high-concurrency tenants to dedicated pools for 24 hours (rolled until 2027-12-01 02:00 UTC).

Root cause (short): a new LRU-adaptive eviction change + an interaction with a workload spike caused the in-memory KV hit-rate to drop, producing repeated recomputation and greater latency amplification at the tail. Full analysis in attached postmortem.

Action items (owners & ask):
1) Marissa — finalize the RCA section + technical slide w/key traces (ETA EOD 12/06).
2) Hannah — confirm SLA math and delta slide for QBR (include lost SLA minutes and customer-facing summary) (ETA 12/07).
3) Vivek — add executive-level framing and cost impact (token-cost delta) for the QBR slide (ETA 12/07).
4) Laura — confirm JIRA rollup and ship timeline for fix->hardening (JIRA keys listed below) (ETA 12/08).
5) Stephanie (me) — compile slides, customer note draft for Acme, and final exec summary for QBR (target 12/09 morning).

Asks: please reply with a one-line confirmation if you can own the items above and confirm ETAs. If you have edits to the postmortem, add inline comments on the Drive doc linked below — I'll incorporate and send the final packet to Vivek for sign-off.

Files attached: 20271205-postmortem-kvcache.pdf (postmortem draft), latency-traces-20271130.png (tail traces).

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Product Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Confirmed — I will own the RCA writeup + technical slide. Notes for the packet:
- Root cause: unintended side-effect of LRU-adaptive threshold under a correlated workload spike (see section 2.2 in doc).
- Customer visible: 3 tenants experienced transient timeouts; Acme had elevated error rates (~0.6% requests affected) primarily on the high-concurrency search path.
- Remediation plan (next steps beyond hotfix):
  * Ship a conservative eviction policy by 12/12 (JIRA-RED-7123).
  * Add KV shadowing to detect hit-rate regressions in preprod by 12/20 (JIRA-RED-7189).

I uploaded the postmortem draft to Drive and attached the PDF and trace PNG here. Also flagged a cost/ops note — the dedicated routing added approximately $1.2k of GPU pool spend during the 42-minute window (rough estimate).

Also recommend CS outreach to Acme with the incident gist and proposed mitigations — that should be a joint message from me + CS lead.

-Marissa
